thread:
alex: Heads-up — I need to swap out as primary in ~10m. Meeting ran long. Leaving maria as primary unless someone objects. Quick status: inference errors spiked ~00:40 UTC, ~5% 5xx across hosted API, latency also up on p50.

maria: ack, will take it. can you drop quick pointers for the handoff? any active paging or customer impact we should call out?

oncall-bot: [INCIDENT] Pager triggered: inference-5xx-rate-high (severity: high) — triggered at 1718501160 — pages: @maria @alex — incident channel: #incidents — runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/inference-5xx

sasha: fwiw saw a small fleet of hosts hitting oom during KV cache writes, might be related to a rolling quantization job earlier. tracing now.

alex: key handoff notes:
- customer impact: some customers seeing 5xx; spike concentrated in model-group: gpt-13-small, regional: us-west-2
- mitigation tried so far: disabled autoscaling burst for the group, rolled back recent quantization rollout to v2 -> v1 (via runtime rollback), bumped request timeout from 30s -> 45s for canary route
- what worked temporarily: routing ~20% of traffic to 'gpt-13-small-fallback' reduced 5xx to ~1.2%

maria: thanks. priorities for next 30m?

alex: list: 
1) confirm full rollback succeeded (check model-server logs and model version in route config)
2) clear prefix/KV cache for the affected model group (helps stuck kv writes)
3) restart any model-server pods with high oom count (graceful drains)
4) if 5xx stays >2%, shift traffic to fallback variant and open emergency scaling to add 2 more GPU workers
5) notify affected customers via status page if sustained >5min

jamal: I can help with node restarts and scaling. Maria, want me to bump capacity now or wait until rollback confirmation?

maria: please wait for rollback confirmation. Sasha — can you post the trace link once you have it? I want the error signature and stack.

sasha: posted: https://telemetry.redwood/p/trace/8a7f3c (error: kv_write_timeout -> downstream model-server busy)

ops-runbook-bot: Quick remediation steps for inference-5xx-rate-high: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/inference-5xx#quick-steps
- Step A: Confirm model route uses expected version: `redwood route get --model gpt-13-small`
- Step B: Drain and restart failing pods: `kubectl drain <pod> && kubectl delete pod <pod>` (pods will be recreated with healthy status)
- Step C: Clear prefix cache (script): `./tools/clear_kv_cache --model gpt-13-small --region us-west-2`
- Step D: Fallback routing: `redwood route update --name gpt-13-small --split fallback=0.25,primary=0.75`

maria: ok I'm running Step A and C now. Alex, leaving the meeting in 3m, will ping once I verify. Jamal — hold off on node restarts until I call it.

alex: +1 on not restarting unless needed. Also flag for postmortem: why did the quantization job touch live deployments? was the rollout pinned?

oncall-bot: [NOTICE] Maria is now primary (swapped by alex at 1718501400) — oncall window: 1718501400 -> 1718526000

maria: Step A: route shows v1 active, rollback completed on control plane side. Step C: cleared KV cache for 6 prefixes; observed drop in 5xx from 5% -> 2.1% over the last 60s.

sasha: logs show repeated `kv write timeout` and then `worker stuck` on 3 pods (pod-12, pod-19, pod-23). suspects: kernel oom_killer or runaway mem spike after quantization.

jamal: I tagged those pods and checking metrics now. mem usage 97% on pod-19, 94% on pod-12. pod-23 intermittently hitting high cpu. I'd recommend draining pod-19 first.

maria: go ahead with drain on pod-19, set bounce to recreate with no local cache. Use graceful drain and preserve connections for 30s.

jamal: running: `kubectl drain pod-19 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30` — will then `kubectl delete pod pod-19` to force recreation.

ops-runbook-bot: Reminder: notify customers if error rate > 3% for >10min. Status page template: https://redwood.internal/status/templates/inference-degraded.md

maria: after pod-19 bounce, error rate down to 1.4% and latency p95 improving. Leaving fallback split at 20% for extra cushion.

alex: thanks all. I'll follow up for the postmortem and add the quantization rollout checklist (we should never touch live canary without stage validation).

sasha: taking note for root-cause — capturing full heap dump from pod-12 and will store at s3://incidents/1718501234/heap-dumps/

maria: summary for handoff: 
- primary: maria (now)
- secondary: jamal (on-call backup)
- active mitigations: rollback quantization -> confirmed, KV cache cleared, pod-19 bounced, fallback routing 20%
- next steps: collect heap dumps, run full canary in staging for quantization job, schedule postmortem and follow-up action items

alex: leaving now. ping if anything spikes, I can jump back in.

maria: thanks alex. I'll keep the thread updated. tagging ops-runbook-bot to close this incident once metrics hold for 30m.

ops-runbook-bot: Incident watch started. Will close when 5xx < 1% for 30m and latency stable.

maria: closing notes: if anyone picks this up later, runbook links: 
- primary runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/inference-5xx
- cache clear tool: https://redwood.internal/tools/clear_kv_cache
- emergency scaling play: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/emergency-scaling

jamal: ack. I'll stay on standby as secondary for the next hour.
